series_items.subject: [PATCH 03/60] mm: introduce the common-memory node state
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new concept in the Linux kernel called 'common-memory nodes' to distinguish between nodes that have memory and those whose memory can be managed by the kernel's memory management services. The existing N_MEMORY flag is overloaded, so it now only indicates whether a node has memory, while a new flag N_MEMORY_COMMON is introduced for common-memory nodes. Userspace can identify these nodes using the 'has_common_memory' attribute. Additionally, documentation is updated to reflect these changes.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that N_MEMORY is overloaded with two meanings, and requested the introduction of N_MEMORY_COMMON to mean nodes whose memory ordinary allocations may use without requesting the node explicitly, and that kernel memory management services manage.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

N_MEMORY is overloaded with two meanings:
  1) a node has memory.
  2) a node's memory is reachable via ordinary allocation or
     an arbitrary MM service may use that memory.

Allow N_MEMORY to mean #1, and introduce N_MEMORY_COMMON to mean #2.

N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes contain "common memory" capable of being managed
arbitrarily by the kernel MM based solely on zone membership. Following
commits convert relevant N_MEMORY users to N_MEMORY_COMMON.

Expose the state via `has_common_memory` so userspace can identify
the memory available to ordinary allocations and common MM services.

Add has_memory to the docs while we're here.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

+

 Date:		October 2002
 Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>
@@ -29,6 +38,14 @@ Description:
 		Nodes that have regular or high memory.
 		Depends on CONFIG_HIGHMEM.
 
+What:		/sys/devices/system/node/has_common_memory
+Date:		November 2026
+Contact:	Linux Memory Management list <linux-mm@kvack.org>

+		Nodes whose memory ordinary allocations may use without
+		requesting the node explicitly, and that kernel memory
+		management services manage.
+
 What:		/sys/devices/system/node/nodeX

   The node has regular or high memory. When ``CONFIG_HIGHMEM`` is disabled

-  The node has memory(regular, high, movable)

+``N_MEMORY_COMMON``

+  memory.
 ``N_CPU``
   The node has one or more CPUs
 ``N_GENERIC_INITIATOR``
@@ -184,6 +189,7 @@ For example, for node 2 with normal memory and CPUs, bit 2 will be set in ::
   node_states[N_NORMAL_MEMORY]

 #endif

+	[N_MEMORY_COMMON] = _NODE_ATTR(has_common_memory, N_MEMORY_COMMON),

index 90bdcffa42ea..c3b984105bd1 100644
--- a/include/linux/nodemask.h
+++ b/include/linux/nodemask.h
@@ -398,7 +398,14 @@ enum node_states {
 #else
 	N_HIGH_MEMORY = N_NORMAL_MEMORY,
 #endif
-	N_MEMORY,		/* The node has memory(regular, high, movable) */
+	/*
+	 * N_MEMORY indicates online memory exists on the node - it is used
+	 * to manage per-node meta-data and topology decisions.
+	 * N_MEMORY_COMMON indicates whether the node can satisfy arbitrary
+	 * allocations and whether a service should manage that node's folios.
+	 */
+	N_MEMORY,		/* the node has memory */
+	N_MEMORY_COMMON,	/* common pool (fallback zonelist) */
 	N_CPU,		/* The node has one or more cpus */
 	N_GENERIC_INITIATOR,	/* The node has one or more Generic Initiators */
 	NR_NODE_STATES
diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index 88d507f93b1a..ddb04b72a160 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -203,6 +203,7 @@ nodemask_t node_states[NR_NODE_STATES] __read_mostly = {
 	[N_HIGH_MEMORY] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
 #endif
 	[N_MEMORY] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
+	[N_MEMORY_COMMON] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
 	[N_CPU] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
 #endif	/* NUMA */
 };
@@ -211,10 +212,12 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL(node_states);
 void __meminit node_set_memory_state(int nid)
 {
 	node_set_state(nid, N_MEMORY);
+	node_set_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON);
 }
 
 void __meminit node_clear_memory_state(int nid)

+	node_clear_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON);
 	node_clear_state(nid, N_MEMORY);

series_items.subject: [PATCH 04/60] mm/page_alloc: build zonelists from common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the build_zonelists() function to construct zonelists from common memory, reducing unnecessary allocations and improving performance. It achieves this by building fallback zonelists from N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes and local-only zonelists for common nodes. The build_local_zonelist() refactor allows for code reuse in constructing a local-only zonelist for nodes outside the N_MEMORY_COMMON set.

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (Meta)

series_items.subject: [PATCH 05/60] mm/mempolicy: keep interleave and tmpfs mount policies on common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory policy module to use a new concept called N_MEMORY_COMMON when calculating boot policies and their per-node sysfs entries. It restricts the node set for mpol_set_nodemask() and mbind() masks to only include nodes that are part of N_MEMORY_COMMON. Additionally, it updates tmpfs and interleave policies to default to common memory nodes if no specific nodelist is provided. This change aims to simplify policy management by limiting the scope of certain policies to a smaller set of nodes.

series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts the demotion topology to common memory by changing various functions in mm/memory-tiers.c to use N_MEMORY_COMMON instead of N_MEMORY. This change aims to prevent nodes outside N_MEMORY_COMMON from being used as generic demotion sources or destinations, and to improve performance by building demotion paths and default DRAM references only from nodes within N_MEMORY_COMMON.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 08/60] mm/migrate: reject move_pages() destinations outside common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the move_pages() function by rejecting destinations outside common memory, ensuring that user memory is placed on a node chosen by the caller and adhering to general-purpose memory policies.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 09/60] mm/damon: reject migration destinations outside common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the DAMOS migration actions to reject destinations outside common memory, aligning with the behavior of move_pages(2). The change involves updating a condition in damon_migrate_pages() to check for N_MEMORY_COMMON instead of N_MEMORY.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 10/60] sched/numa: restrict NUMA migration targets to common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series aims to restrict NUMA migration targets to common memory, addressing a limitation in the current implementation where migrations to nodes without local memory can fail. The change involves updating the should_numa_migrate_memory() function to check for N_MEMORY_COMMON instead of N_MEMORY. This modification ensures that folios are not migrated to nodes with empty __GFP_THISNODE zonelists, preventing potential failures and isolations.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 11/60] fork: check cached stack locality only on common memory nodes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the try_release_thread_stack_to_cache() function to skip checking stack locality when the local node has no common memory. This change allows CPUs on nodes outside N_MEMORY_COMMON to cache stacks from other nodes, improving performance.

series_items.patch_summary: This patch series aims to restrict reclaim operations to common memory nodes, improving the efficiency of memory management in Linux. The changes involve modifying kswapd and direct reclaim to only operate on common nodes, using first_node_state() and next_node_state() instead of first_memory_node and next_memory_node. This approach is expected to reduce unnecessary reclaim activities and improve system performance.

series_items.patch_summary: This patch series aims to optimize memory allocation and deallocation in the Linux kernel by introducing a new approach for counting common memory nodes during kswapd recovery. The goal is to improve system performance and reduce memory fragmentation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 16/60] mm/oom_kill: compare OOM constraints against common memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses OOM (Out of Memory) handling in the Linux kernel by comparing policy and cpuset constraints against common memory nodes. The goal is to prevent nodes outside common memory from inflating constrained capacity or making global policies appear constrained.

The changes modify functions such as `count_free_highmem_pages` and `hibernate_preallocate_memory` to only count free pages on nodes with N_MEMORY_COMMON state.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 23/60] mm/damon: restrict DAMON-native folio operations to common memory

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

A private request allocates only from its node's private zonelist. If
the cpuset revokes the node, or memory hotplug removes it, the request
has nowhere left to allocate, and a faulting task retries forever.

An ordinary bind policy does not hit this. A cpuset change rebinds it,
and check_retry_cpuset() drops a nodemask that no longer intersects the
cpuset. A private binding is never rebound, and dropping its nodemask
does not help, since the private zonelist still holds only its node.

Add relax_private_alloc() as the last of the slowpath retry checks.
When no node in a private request's zonelist is in its nodemask and
allowed by the cpuset, it drops ALLOC_ZONELIST_PRIVATE and the nodemask
and switches to the common zonelist of the preferred node, which
alloc_context now records. It runs after check_retry_cpuset() and
check_retry_zonelist(), so a concurrent update retries with the original
constraints instead.

A node counts in any zone type, so a GFP zone restriction or an
exhausted node never relaxes a request. A __GFP_THISNODE private request
is never relaxed. check_retry_cpuset() leaves a private request's
nodemask alone.

The alloc_context comment now lists nodemask and alloc_flags among the
fields the slowpath may change.

Without private nodes, the slowpath retry checks are unchanged.

series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new internal node state called N_MEMORY_COMPACTION to the Linux kernel. This state indicates that the kernel can compact memory on its own initiative for the given node. The patch also updates various files, including documentation and code, to reflect this new state. The addition of this state allows the kernel to more efficiently manage memory compaction across different nodes in the system.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the addition of N_MEMORY_COMPACTION to enum node_states requires updating the BUILD_BUG_ON checks in drivers/base/node.c and include/linux/nodemask.h, as well as adding a new bit to NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_ALL.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

Add N_MEMORY_COMPACTION for the nodes compaction may operate on, and
NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMPACTION for memory providers to select it.

Common memory carries every feature, so a mask with
NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON must now include compaction.

The state is internal and has no sysfs file. Internal states follow
N_GENERIC_INITIATOR, so check sysfs coverage only for the states up to
it.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst |  7 +++++++
 drivers/base/node.c                  |  5 +++--
 include/linux/nodemask.h             | 20 ++++++++++++++++----
 mm/page_alloc.c                      |  4 ++++
 4 files changed, 30 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

diff --git a/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst b/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst
index ddba7c890418..5d0a69f6c23c 100644
--- a/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst
+++ b/Documentation/mm/physical_memory.rst
@@ -182,6 +182,12 @@ nodes with particular properties as defined by ``enum node_states``:
 ``N_GENERIC_INITIATOR``
   The node has one or more Generic Initiators
 
+The following states are internal and not exported through sysfs:
+
+``N_MEMORY_COMPACTION``
+  The kernel compacts the node on its own initiative (kcompactd, proactive
+  and explicit compaction).
+
 For each node that has a property described above, the bit corresponding to the
 node ID in the ``node_states[<property>]`` bitmask is set.
 
@@ -194,6 +200,7 @@ For example, for node 2 with normal memory and CPUs, bit 2 will be set in ::
   node_states[N_MEMORY]
   node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON]
   node_states[N_CPU]
+  node_states[N_MEMORY_COMPACTION]
 
 For various operations possible with nodemasks please refer to
 ``include/linux/nodemask.h``.
diff --git a/drivers/base/node.c b/drivers/base/node.c
index 56a1741a6a45..19f93cda90be 100644
--- a/drivers/base/node.c
+++ b/drivers/base/node.c
@@ -1000,8 +1000,9 @@ void __init node_dev_init(void)
 {
 	int ret, i;
 
- 	BUILD_BUG_ON(ARRAY_SIZE(node_state_attr) != NR_NODE_STATES);
- 	BUILD_BUG_ON(ARRAY_SIZE(node_state_attrs)-1 != NR_NODE_STATES);
+	/* Node states after N_GENERIC_INITIATOR have no sysfs file. */
+	BUILD_BUG_ON(ARRAY_SIZE(node_state_attr) != N_GENERIC_INITIATOR + 1);
+	BUILD_BUG_ON(ARRAY_SIZE(node_state_attrs)-1 != N_GENERIC_INITIATOR + 1);
 
 	ret = subsys_system_register(&node_subsys, cpu_root_attr_groups);
 	if (ret)
diff --git a/include/linux/nodemask.h b/include/linux/nodemask.h
index 02908ef23a62..2757acffff2b 100644
--- a/include/linux/nodemask.h
+++ b/include/linux/nodemask.h
@@ -411,6 +411,8 @@ enum node_states {
 	N_MEMORY_PRIVATE,	/* memory outside the common pool */
 	N_CPU,		/* The node has one or more cpus */
 	N_GENERIC_INITIATOR,	/* The node has one or more Generic Initiators */
+	/* Internal states, not exported through sysfs */
+	N_MEMORY_COMPACTION,	/* mm compaction may operate on the node */
 	NR_NODE_STATES
 };
 
@@ -542,16 +544,26 @@ static __always_inline int node_random(const nodemask_t *maskp)
 #define for_each_online_node(node) for_each_node_state(node, N_ONLINE)
 #define for_each_node_with_cpus(node)	for_each_node_state(node, N_CPU)
 
-/* Private nodes omit NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON. */
+/*
+ * Private nodes omit NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON. Their providers opt into
+ * individual MM services with the remaining bits.
+ */
 #define NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON		BIT(0) /* add to fallback zonelist */
-#define NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_ALL		NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON
+#define NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMPACTION	BIT(1) /* mm compaction */
+#define NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_ALL		(NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON | \
+					 NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMPACTION)
 
-/* Private memory needs NUMA: node 0 holds all memory without it. */
+/*
+ * Common memory carries every feature. Private memory needs NUMA: node 0
+ * holds all memory without it.
+ */
 static inline bool node_memory_features_valid(unsigned long features)
 {
 	if (features & ~NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_ALL)
 		return false;
-	return IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_NUMA) || (features & NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON);
+	if (features & NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON)
+		return features == NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_ALL;
+	return IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_NUMA);
 }
 
 /*
diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index b7339bc634d5..335ce73e645e 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -204,6 +204,7 @@ nodemask_t node_states[NR_NODE_STATES] __read_mostly = {
 #endif
 	[N_MEMORY] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
 	[N_MEMORY_COMMON] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
+	[N_MEMORY_COMPACTION] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
 	[N_CPU] = { { [0] = 1UL } },
 #endif	/* NUMA */
 };
@@ -218,10 +219,13 @@ void __meminit node_set_memory_state(int nid, unsigned long features)
 		node_set_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON);
 	else
 		node_set_state(nid, N_MEMORY_PRIVATE);
+	if (features & NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMPACTION)
+		node_set_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMPACTION);
 }
 
 void __meminit node_clear_memory_state(int nid)
 {
+	node_clear_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMPACTION);
 	node_clear_state(nid, N_MEMORY_PRIVATE);
 	node_clear_state(nid, N_MEMORY_COMMON);
 	node_clear_state(nid, N_MEMORY);

--

series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts compaction to N_MEMORY_COMPACTION instead of common memory, affecting proactive compaction and kcompactd initialization.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 46/60] mm: add N_MEMORY_RECLAIM node state
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new internal state for Linux nodes called N_MEMORY_RECLAIM, which indicates that the kernel can reclaim memory from the node on its own initiative. It also introduces a new feature flag NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_RECLAIM for memory providers to select this capability. The patch ensures that private nodes that permit reclaim must also permit compaction, as reclaim frees order-0 pages and leaves high-order requests to compaction.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the addition of N_MEMORY_RECLAIM node state and NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_RECLAIM feature does not account for lock ordering between reclaim paths and compaction, suggesting that the per-vswap spinlock should be dropped before calling try_to_unmap().

  */
 #define NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON		BIT(0) /* add to fallback zonelist */
 #define NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMPACTION	BIT(1) /* mm compaction */

 #define NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_ALL		(NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_COMMON | \

series_items.subject: [PATCH 47/60] mm/vmscan: restrict reclaim to N_MEMORY_RECLAIM instead of N_MEMORY_COMMON
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts the reclaim process to nodes that have opted into it by setting the N_MEMORY_RECLAIM state, rather than serving all common memory. This change affects kswapd and its interfaces, as well as watermark management and direct reclaim. Private nodes that permit reclaim will now get watermarks again and be boosted, while those without this state keep zero watermarks. The patch also updates various functions to reflect these changes, including si_mem_available() and the hopeless-kswapd recovery on page free.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Gregory Relay noted that the patch restricts reclaim to N_MEMORY_RECLAIM nodes by modifying various functions in mm/vmscan.c, but did not provide any specific feedback or suggestions for improvement.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 48/60] mm/madvise: restrict reclaim advice to reclaim-capable memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series restricts the reclaim advice to only common memory nodes, introducing a new function `folio_allows_reclaim()` that checks if a folio's node permits reclaim. The changes are made in various files related to madvise and huge pages.

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (Meta)
review_comments.summary: The original patch author posted a duplicate message with no changes or discussion.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 49/60] mm/vmscan: reclaim private nodes for memcg
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue in the memcg (memory cgroup) reclaim mechanism, where private nodes that permit reclaim are not being scanned for memory usage over their limit. The patch introduces a new function `zonelist_reaches_node` to check if a node is reachable through the zonelist, and uses this function to identify private nodes that need to be reclaimed. This ensures that memcg reclaim covers all nodes that permit reclaim, including those not covered by the zonelist. The patch modifies the `shrink_zones` function to include these additional nodes in the reclaim process.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch does not cover private nodes in memcg reclaim, and suggested visiting these nodes after the zonelist to give them the same refault snapshot and congestion reset.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 50/60] mm: add N_MEMORY_MEMPOLICY node state
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new internal node state called N_MEMORY_MEMPOLICY, which allows memory policy interfaces and explicit migration to target specific nodes. It also introduces a new feature flag NODE_MEMORY_FEAT_MEMPOLICY for memory providers to select this feature. The feature requires both reclaim and compaction of the node, and userspace placement can use the node like any other memory. This patch is part of a larger series of changes and is intended to improve NUMA control and memory management in Linux.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch adds a new node state for memory policy interfaces and explicit migration, but failed to update the node_memory_features_valid() function to check for this feature.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 51/60] mm: restrict explicit migration to N_MEMORY_MEMPOLICY
series_items.patch_summary: This patch restricts explicit migration to N_MEMORY_MEMPOLICY nodes, allowing userspace NUMA operations to target these nodes. It introduces a new function `folio_allows_mempolicy()` that checks if a folio's node permits memory policy and uses it instead of the existing functions. The patch also updates cpuset migration to evacuate private memory only from nodes the cpuset no longer allows.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 52/60] mm: count memory with userspace placement as general purpose
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory accounting to treat memory on nodes that can be used by userspace as general-purpose memory. This means that totalram_pages() and MemFree will count this memory, and it will also affect other metrics such as overcommit and OOM capacity. The patch introduces new functions common_free_pages() and common_file_pages() to accurately calculate the amount of free memory on these nodes. It also adjusts the calculation of global dirtyable memory to exclude private memory that serves only private bindings and migration.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Gregory Relay noted that the patch incorrectly uses common_free_pages() in global_dirtyable_memory(), which counts private memory as well, and suggested using nr_free_pages() instead to accurately count only free pages on common nodes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 53/60] mm/mempolicy: add MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES for private node bindings
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new flag, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES, to the Linux kernel's memory policy system. The flag allows users to bind a process's memory to a private node, which behaves differently from ordinary bindings by being strict and never rebound. Private nodes are ignored in the absence of this flag. The patch also updates various functions and documentation to support this new behavior.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the documentation for MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES does not clearly explain how it interacts with HugeTLB mappings, and requested clarification on whether this flag can be used on HugeTLB mappings.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 54/60] mm/migrate: route explicit NUMA migration to private nodes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory migration functionality to allow explicit NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) migration to private nodes. Currently, private nodes are not reachable through the standard allocation mechanism due to their unique zonelist configuration. The patch introduces a new flag, ALLOC_ZONELIST_PRIVATE, which enables the use of the private zonelist for allocation when migrating pages to a private node. This change affects the move_pages and migrate_pages system calls, as well as the alloc_migration_target function. Additionally, HugeTLB folios are still excluded from migration to private nodes due to their specific memory characteristics.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that private nodes are only reachable through their private zonelist, and requested the use of ALLOC_ZONELIST_PRIVATE flag in alloc_migration_target() when migrating to a private node.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 55/60] mm/memory_hotplug: online and offline private memory nodes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows a driver to hotplug memory onto a private node at runtime by passing a feature mask through driver-managed hotplug. The patch rejects masks that are not valid according to the node_memory_features_valid() function. Memory joins a node only if it has the same feature mask as the node, and the node's features remain until all System RAM blocks are removed, even when ZONE_DEVICE memory keeps the node alive. This patch also introduces a new function can_claim_node_memory() that checks whether a node can claim its memory based on the provided feature mask.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch does not check if a memory block belongs to multiple nodes before calling can_claim_node_memory(), which may lead to incorrect results.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 56/60] dax/kmem: add a private memory mode
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a private memory mode to the dax/kmem driver, allowing userspace to target specific capacity as private memory. The private attribute is exposed through sysfs and defaults to false. When set to true, the memory is onlined with features that enable reclaim and compaction management, excluding it from ordinary allocations and other memory management services. Userspace can bind anonymous and shmem-backed mappings to this private memory using a single-node mbind policy. The attribute is hidden without CONFIG_NUMA or CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE configurations.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the private attribute is not properly protected against concurrent access, and suggested adding a lock to protect it.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 57/60] selftests/dax: test private kmem devices and services
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds tests to verify the 'private' attribute of kmem devices and services across memory hotplug events. The tests check that private memory can be unplugged, that the mode changes only while unplugged, and that online common memory cannot become private. Additionally, the tests ensure that services such as kswapd and kcompactd run correctly on a private node, and that HugeTLB pool growth stays off the node.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the kswapd and kcompactd services are not properly stopped on a private node before attempting to reclaim memory, which can lead to unexpected behavior. The reviewer suggested adding calls to stop these services before running the reclaim paths.

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

Test dax/kmem private mode on a device-dax instance:
  - the private attribute across memory hotplug: private memory joins
    has_private_memory, the mode changes only while unplugged, and
    online common memory cannot become private.
  - services on the private node: kswapd and kcompactd run,
    nodeN/reclaim and nodeN/compact are accepted, and HugeTLB pool
    growth stays off the node.

The tests reconfigure a device, so they run only when DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV
names one (daxX.Y), or is "auto" to pick a device whose memory is not
online. The device's original configuration is restored on exit.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

+#!/bin/bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+#
+# Exercise the kmem "private" attribute across memory hotplug: when it may
+# change, and whether onlined memory joins has_private_memory or
+# has_common_memory.
+#
+# Needs root and DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV=<daxX.Y|auto>, see private_node_common.sh.
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC1091
+DIR="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
+. "$DIR"/../kselftest/ktap_helpers.sh
+. "$DIR"/private_node_common.sh
+
+trap pn_unbind_kmem_private EXIT
+pn_setup
+
+if ! echo unplugged > "$D/state" 2>/dev/null ||
+   pn_node_in "$PN" has_memory; then
+	ktap_exit_fail_msg "private memory cannot be unplugged"
+fi
+
+ktap_set_plan 8
+
+name="private mode can be selected while unplugged"
+if echo 0 > "$D/private" 2>/dev/null && echo 1 > "$D/private" 2>/dev/null &&
+   [ "$(cat "$D/private")" = 1 ]; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="invalid private setting is rejected"
+if ! echo invalid > "$D/private" 2>/dev/null &&
+   [ "$(cat "$D/private")" = 1 ]; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="private online publishes private memory"
+if echo online_movable > "$D/state" 2>/dev/null &&
+   pn_node_is_private "$PN" && ! pn_node_in "$PN" has_common_memory; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+# Writing the current value again is accepted.
+name="private mode cannot change while memory blocks exist"
+if ! echo 0 > "$D/private" 2>/dev/null &&
+   [ "$(cat "$D/private")" = 1 ] && echo 1 > "$D/private" 2>/dev/null; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="unplug removes the private node from memory lists"
+if echo unplugged > "$D/state" 2>/dev/null &&
+   ! pn_node_in "$PN" has_memory &&
+   ! pn_node_in "$PN" has_private_memory; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="common mode preserves normal kmem behavior"
+if echo 0 > "$D/private" 2>/dev/null &&
+   echo online_movable > "$D/state" 2>/dev/null &&
+   pn_node_in "$PN" has_common_memory; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="online common memory cannot be reclassified as private"
+if ! echo 1 > "$D/private" 2>/dev/null &&
+   [ "$(cat "$D/private")" = 0 ]; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="private mode can be restored through an unplug cycle"
+if echo unplugged > "$D/state" 2>/dev/null &&
+   echo 1 > "$D/private" 2>/dev/null &&
+   echo online_movable > "$D/state" 2>/dev/null &&
+   pn_node_is_private "$PN"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+ktap_finished

+#!/bin/bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+#
+# Check which MM services a private kmem node gets: no HugeTLB pool pages,
+# but kswapd, kcompactd and per-node compaction and reclaim.
+#
+# Needs root and DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV=<daxX.Y|auto>, see private_node_common.sh.
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC1091
+DIR="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
+. "$DIR"/../kselftest/ktap_helpers.sh
+. "$DIR"/private_node_common.sh
+
+trap pn_unbind_kmem_private EXIT
+pn_setup
+
+ktap_set_plan 5
+
+# Use the default size: a gigantic page may not fit the device at all.
+hsize=$(awk '/^Hugepagesize:/ { print $2 }' /proc/meminfo)
+pool="$NODE_BASE/node$PN/hugepages/hugepages-${hsize}kB/nr_hugepages"
+global=/sys/kernel/mm/hugepages/hugepages-${hsize}kB/nr_hugepages
+name_node="per-node HugeTLB pool growth skips private memory"
+name_global="HugeTLB pool growth falls back to other nodes"
+if [ -z "$hsize" ] || [ ! -w "$pool" ] || [ ! -w "$global" ]; then
+	ktap_print_msg "HugeTLB pools unavailable"
+	ktap_test_skip "$name_node"
+	ktap_test_skip "$name_global"
+else
+	before=$(cat "$pool")
+	echo $((before + 8)) > "$pool" 2>/dev/null
+	after=$(cat "$pool")
+	echo "$before" > "$pool" 2>/dev/null
+	if [ "$after" = "$before" ]; then
+		ktap_test_pass "$name_node"
+	else
+		ktap_print_msg "private-node pool grew $before->$after"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name_node"
+	fi
+
+	gbefore=$(cat "$global")
+	echo $((gbefore + 64)) > "$global" 2>/dev/null
+	gafter=$(cat "$global")
+	after=$(cat "$pool")
+	echo "$gbefore" > "$global" 2>/dev/null
+	if [ "$gafter" -le "$gbefore" ]; then
+		ktap_print_msg "HugeTLB pool could not grow on any node"
+		ktap_test_skip "$name_global"
+	elif [ "$after" = "$before" ]; then
+		ktap_test_pass "$name_global"
+	else
+		ktap_print_msg "private-node pool grew $before->$after"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name_global"
+	fi
+fi
+
+compact="$NODE_BASE/node$PN/compact"
+name="kswapd and kcompactd run for the private node"
+if ! pgrep -x "kswapd$PN" >/dev/null; then
+	ktap_print_msg "kswapd$PN is not running"
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+elif [ ! -e "$compact" ]; then
+	ktap_print_msg "kcompactd unavailable without compaction"
+	ktap_test_skip "$name"
+elif pgrep -x "kcompactd$PN" >/dev/null; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_print_msg "kcompactd$PN is not running"
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="private-node compaction is accepted"
+if [ ! -e "$compact" ]; then
+	ktap_print_msg "per-node compaction unavailable"
+	ktap_test_skip "$name"
+elif echo 1 > "$compact" 2>/dev/null; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+reclaim="$NODE_BASE/node$PN/reclaim"
+name="private-node reclaim is accepted"
+if [ ! -e "$reclaim" ]; then
+	ktap_print_msg "per-node reclaim unavailable"
+	ktap_test_skip "$name"
+elif err=$(export LC_ALL=C; echo 1M 2>&1 > "$reclaim"); then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+elif [[ $err == *"Resource temporarily unavailable"* ]]; then
+	# An idle node may have nothing to reclaim.
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_print_msg "$err"
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+ktap_finished

--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/dax/private_node_common.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,208 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+# shellcheck shell=bash disable=SC2034
+# Helpers shared by the kmem_private*.sh selftests, sourced after
+# ../kselftest/ktap_helpers.sh.
+#
+# DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV=<daxX.Y|auto> opts into reconfiguring a device-dax
+# instance as private kmem memory. "auto" only uses devices whose memory is
+# not online and that no process has open or mapped. A named device is used
+# whatever its state. Either is restored on exit.
+#
+# pn_setup() sets D to the sysfs directory of that device and PN to its node.
+
+DAX_BASE=/sys/bus/dax/devices
+NODE_BASE=/sys/devices/system/node
+
+# Whether nodelist $1 (e.g. "0-2,4") contains node $2.
+pn_nodelist_has()
+{
+	local nid=$2 token low high
+
+	for token in ${1//,/ }; do
+		low=${token%-*}
+		high=${token#*-}
+		if [ "$nid" -ge "$low" ] 2>/dev/null &&
+		   [ "$nid" -le "$high" ] 2>/dev/null; then
+			return 0
+		fi
+	done
+	return 1
+}
+
+# Whether node $1 is in the node state list $2, e.g. has_memory.
+pn_node_in()
+{
+	[ -r "$NODE_BASE/$2" ] &&
+		pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$NODE_BASE/$2")" "$1"
+}
+
+pn_node_is_private()
+{
+	pn_node_in "$1" has_private_memory
+}
+
+# Whether any process has device node $1 open or mapped.
+pn_dev_in_use()
+{
+	local fd
+
+	for fd in /proc/[0-9]*/fd/*; do
+		[ "$(readlink "$fd" 2>/dev/null)" = "$1" ] && return 0
+	done
+	grep -qs " $1\$" /proc/[0-9]*/maps
+}
+
+# Record the original configuration of device $1, bound to driver $2, for
+# pn_unbind_kmem_private().
+pn_record_kmem()
+{
+	# Binding the recorded device again keeps its original configuration.
+	[ "${PN_DEV:-}" != "$1" ] || return 0
+	PN_DEV=$1
+	PN_ORIG_DRIVER=$2
+	PN_ORIG_STATE=$(cat "$1/state" 2>/dev/null)
+	PN_ORIG_PRIVATE=$(cat "$1/private" 2>/dev/null)
+	PN_NEW_ID=
+}
+
+# Move device $1 from driver $2 to kmem and online it as private memory on
+# node $3.
+pn_online_private()
+{
+	local dev=$1 driver=$2 nid=$3 name
+
+	name=$(basename "$dev")
+	if [ "$driver" = kmem ]; then
+		echo unplugged > "$dev/state" || return 1
+	elif [ -n "$driver" ]; then
+		echo "$name" > "/sys/bus/dax/drivers/$driver/unbind" || return 1
+	fi
+	# A private node holds the memory of this device only.
+	if pn_node_in "$nid" has_memory; then
+		return 1
+	fi
+	if [ "$driver" != kmem ]; then
+		echo "$name" > /sys/bus/dax/drivers/kmem/new_id || return 1
+		PN_NEW_ID=1
+	fi
+	echo unplugged > "$dev/state" &&
+		echo 1 > "$dev/private" &&
+		echo online_movable > "$dev/state" &&
+		pn_node_is_private "$nid"
+}
+
+# Online device $1 as private kmem memory, or return 1 if it is unusable.
+pn_bind_kmem_private()
+{
+	local dev=$1 name driver nid
+
+	name=$(basename "$dev")
+	nid=$(cat "$dev/target_node" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+	driver=$(basename "$(readlink "$dev/driver" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null)
+	if [ "$driver" = kmem ] &&
+	   [ "$(cat "$dev/state" 2>/dev/null)" != unplugged ]; then
+		# Leave online kmem memory alone unless it is ours or was named.
+		if [ "$DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV" = auto ] &&
+		   [ "${PN_DEV:-}" != "$dev" ]; then
+			return 1
+		fi
+		if [ "$(cat "$dev/private" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] &&
+		   pn_node_is_private "$nid"; then
+			pn_record_kmem "$dev" "$driver"
+			return 0
+		fi
+	elif pn_node_in "$nid" has_memory; then
+		return 1
+	elif [ "$DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV" = auto ] && pn_dev_in_use "/dev/$name"; then
+		return 1
+	fi
+
+	pn_record_kmem "$dev" "$driver"
+	if ! pn_online_private "$dev" "$driver" "$nid" 2>/dev/null; then
+		pn_unbind_kmem_private
+		return 1
+	fi
+}
+
+# Restore the device recorded by pn_bind_kmem_private(), if any.
+pn_unbind_kmem_private()
+{
+	local dev=${PN_DEV:-} name
+
+	[ -n "$dev" ] || return 0
+	PN_DEV=
+	name=$(basename "$dev")
+	if [ "$(basename "$(readlink "$dev/driver" 2>/dev/null)")" = kmem ]; then
+		echo unplugged > "$dev/state" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+		if [ -n "$PN_ORIG_PRIVATE" ]; then
+			echo "$PN_ORIG_PRIVATE" > "$dev/private" 2>/dev/null
+		fi
+	fi
+	if [ "$PN_ORIG_DRIVER" = kmem ]; then
+		case "$PN_ORIG_STATE" in
+		unplugged) ;;
+		offline)
+			# kmem cannot restore blocks onlined behind its back.
+			ktap_print_msg "$name was offline and is left unplugged"
+			;;
+		*) echo "$PN_ORIG_STATE" > "$dev/state" 2>/dev/null ;;
+		esac
+		return 0
+	fi
+	if [ -e "$dev/driver" ]; then
+		echo "$name" > /sys/bus/dax/drivers/kmem/unbind 2>/dev/null
+	fi
+	if [ -n "$PN_NEW_ID" ]; then
+		echo "$name" > /sys/bus/dax/drivers/kmem/remove_id 2>/dev/null
+	fi
+	if [ -n "$PN_ORIG_DRIVER" ]; then
+		echo "$name" > "/sys/bus/dax/drivers/$PN_ORIG_DRIVER/bind" \
+			2>/dev/null
+	fi
+	return 0
+}
+
+pn_skip()
+{
+	ktap_skip_all "$1"
+	exit "$KSFT_SKIP"
+}
+
+# An explicitly selected device must provision, auto may find none.
+pn_skip_or_fail()
+{
+	if [ "$DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV" = auto ]; then
+		pn_skip "$1"
+	fi
+	ktap_exit_fail_msg "$1"
+}
+
+# Print the KTAP header, check the prerequisites and bind a private kmem
+# device, setting D and PN.
+pn_setup()
+{
+	local dev nid
+
+	ktap_print_header
+	[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || pn_skip "must be run as root"
+	[ -n "${DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV:-}" ] ||
+		pn_skip "set DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV=<daxX.Y|auto> to select a test device"
+	[ -e "$NODE_BASE/has_private_memory" ] ||
+		pn_skip "kernel lacks private memory nodes"
+	modprobe -q kmem 2>/dev/null
+	[ -d /sys/bus/dax/drivers/kmem ] || pn_skip "dax kmem driver unavailable"
+
+	for dev in "$DAX_BASE"/dax*; do
+		if [ "$DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV" != auto ] &&
+		   [ "$(basename "$dev")" != "$DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV" ]; then
+			continue
+		fi
+		nid=$(cat "$dev/target_node" 2>/dev/null) || continue
+		[ "$nid" -ge 0 ] 2>/dev/null || continue
+		pn_bind_kmem_private "$dev" || continue
+		D=$dev
+		PN=$nid
+		return 0
+	done
+	pn_skip_or_fail "no private kmem device"
+}

--

series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a test to the Linux kernel's selftest suite to verify the memory policy on private nodes. The test uses the kmem_private_policy_tool to report KTAP results, which include testing for private node binding, memory movement, and reclaiming. The test also checks that exhausting private memory fails with a SIGBUS signal and leaves another task on the node alone. The patch raises the dax selftest timeout to 300 seconds due to the policy test faults in node-sized buffers.

The tests cover various scenarios, including policy changes across cpuset.mems, task attachment, hotplug events, and rebind operations. The test suite includes new scripts and tools to simulate these scenarios and verify the behavior of private nodes. The patch also updates the Makefile and configuration files to include the new test programs and dependencies.

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

Test private nodes in cgroup-v2 cpusets with kmem_private_rebind_tool:
  - cpuset.mems may name a private node, a private-only request
    inherits the parent's common nodes, and ordinary allocations in the
    cpuset stay on common memory.
  - policies across cpuset.mems changes and task attachment: interleave
    and positional rebinds never reach private memory, and a private
    binding keeps its node while it is allowed, evacuates to common
    memory when it is revoked, and returns when it is restored.
  - policies across hotplug: a private binding falls back while its
    node is offline or common and resumes once the node is private
    again, and a common binding falls back when its node becomes
    private.

Run with DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV=<daxX.Y|auto>. The rebind tests need two
common memory nodes.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

+#!/bin/bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+#
+# Check that cgroup-v2 cpuset.mems may name a private kmem node without
+# exposing it to ordinary allocations.
+#
+# Needs root, DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV=<daxX.Y|auto> (see private_node_common.sh),
+# one common memory node and the cgroup-v2 cpuset controller.
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC1091
+DIR="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
+. "$DIR"/../kselftest/ktap_helpers.sh
+. "$DIR"/private_node_common.sh
+
+TOOL="$DIR/kmem_private_rebind_tool"
+CG="$CGROOT/kmem-private-cpuset-$$"
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC2317 # invoked by the EXIT trap
+cleanup()
+{
+	pn_cpuset_cleanup "$CG"
+	pn_unbind_kmem_private
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+pn_setup
+[ -x "$TOOL" ] || pn_skip "kmem_private_rebind_tool not built"
+pn_find_common_nodes 1
+pn_require_mask_nodes "$PN" "${COMMON[0]}"
+pn_cpuset_cgroup "$CG"
+
+ktap_set_plan 4
+
+name="mixed common/private cpuset.mems is accepted"
+if echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" 2>/dev/null &&
+   pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems.effective")" "$PN"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="a private-only request keeps the node and inherits common memory"
+if echo "$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" 2>/dev/null &&
+   pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems")" "$PN" &&
+   pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems.effective")" "$PN" &&
+   pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems.effective")" "${COMMON[0]}"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="ordinary allocation in the cpuset stays on common memory"
+out=$(timeout 60 sh -c "echo \$\$ > '$CG/cgroup.procs'; exec '$TOOL' \
+	ordinary '$PN' '${COMMON[0]}' '${COMMON[0]}'")
+if [ "$out" = "private=0" ]; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_print_msg "$out"
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+name="removing the private node revokes it"
+if echo "${COMMON[0]}" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" 2>/dev/null &&
+   ! pn_nodelist_has "$(cat "$CG/cpuset.mems.effective")" "$PN"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+ktap_finished

--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/dax/kmem_private_rebind.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,301 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+#
+# Check memory policies on private kmem memory while a cgroup-v2 cpuset is
+# reshaped, tasks move between cpusets, and the node is hotplugged. Each case
+# starts kmem_private_rebind_tool, changes the cpuset or the node, and sends
+# the tool SIGUSR1 to check where its memory went.
+#
+# Needs root, DAX_KMEM_TEST_DEV=<daxX.Y|auto> (see private_node_common.sh),
+# two common memory nodes and the cgroup-v2 cpuset controller.
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC1091
+DIR="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
+. "$DIR"/../kselftest/ktap_helpers.sh
+. "$DIR"/private_node_common.sh
+
+TOOL="$DIR/kmem_private_rebind_tool"
+CG="$CGROOT/kmem-private-rebind-$$"
+CGCOMMON="$CGROOT/kmem-private-rebind-common-$$"
+OUT=$(mktemp)
+
+# CHILD is the timeout wrapper and TARGET the tool, which may be its child.
+stop_tool()
+{
+	[ -n "${TARGET:-}" ] && kill "$TARGET" 2>/dev/null
+	[ -n "${CHILD:-}" ] && kill "$CHILD" 2>/dev/null
+	[ -n "${CHILD:-}" ] && wait "$CHILD" 2>/dev/null
+	TARGET=
+	CHILD=
+}
+
+# shellcheck disable=SC2317 # invoked by the EXIT trap
+cleanup()
+{
+	stop_tool
+	rm -f "$OUT"
+	pn_cpuset_cleanup "$CG" "$CGCOMMON"
+	pn_unbind_kmem_private
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+wait_output()
+{
+	local pattern=$1 i
+
+	for ((i = 0; i < 100; i++)); do
+		grep -q "$pattern" "$OUT" && return 0
+		kill -0 "$CHILD" 2>/dev/null || break
+		sleep 0.1
+	done
+	return 1
+}
+
+# Start the tool in mode $1, inside cgroup $2 if given, and wait until it is
+# ready for the first SIGUSR1.
+start_tool()
+{
+	local mode=$1 cg=${2:-}
+
+	: > "$OUT"
+	if [ -n "$cg" ]; then
+		timeout 60 sh -ec "echo \$\$ > '$cg/cgroup.procs'; exec '$TOOL' \
+			'$mode' '$PN' '${COMMON[0]}' '${COMMON[1]}'" > "$OUT" 2>&1 &
+	else
+		timeout 60 "$TOOL" "$mode" "$PN" "${COMMON[0]}" "${COMMON[1]}" \
+			> "$OUT" 2>&1 &
+	fi
+	CHILD=$!
+	wait_output '^ready pid=' || return 1
+	TARGET=$(sed -n 's/^ready pid=//p' "$OUT")
+}
+
+# Signal the tool to check stage $1 and report its result as test $2.
+# Returns 1 if the tool did not answer.
+report_stage()
+{
+	local stage=$1 name=$2 line
+
+	if ! kill -USR1 "$TARGET" || ! wait_output "^stage=$stage "; then
+		ktap_print_msg "no answer from the tool"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	line=$(grep "^stage=$stage " "$OUT")
+	ktap_print_msg "$line"
+	if grep -q 'ok=1$' <<<"$line"; then
+		ktap_test_pass "$name"
+	else
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+	fi
+}
+
+# Run task policy mode $1 in the cpuset across one cpuset.mems change. The
+# tool's result is the last line of $OUT.
+run_task_policy()
+{
+	echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	if ! start_tool "$1" "$CG" ||
+	   ! echo "${COMMON[1]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" ||
+	   ! kill -USR1 "$TARGET" || ! wait "$CHILD"; then
+		stop_tool
+		echo "tool failed" >> "$OUT"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	CHILD=
+	TARGET=
+}
+
+# Allow or revoke the private node at stage $2, by attaching the tool to
+# another cpuset or by writing mask $3 to cpuset.mems, for action $1.
+transition_cpuset()
+{
+	local action=$1 stage=$2 mask=$3
+
+	case "$action:$stage" in
+	attach:1) echo "$TARGET" > "$CGCOMMON/cgroup.procs" ;;
+	attach:*) echo "$TARGET" > "$CG/cgroup.procs" ;;
+	*) echo "$mask" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" ;;
+	esac
+}
+
+# A private binding in tool mode $1 while its cpuset allows, revokes and
+# allows the private node again, by action reshape or attach.
+run_private_transitions()
+{
+	local mode=$1 label=$2 action=${3:-reshape}
+	local stage mask title cg=
+	local titles=("keeps private pages and placement while the node stays allowed"
+		"evacuates private pages and uses common placement when access is revoked"
+		"restores the original private request when access returns")
+
+	echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	if [ "$action" = attach ]; then
+		echo "${COMMON[1]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	fi
+	# Shared-policy parents and task-attachment tools start at the root.
+	if [ "$mode" = private-anon ] && [ "$action" = reshape ]; then
+		cg=$CG
+	fi
+	if ! start_tool "$mode" "$cg"; then
+		ktap_print_msg "tool setup failed"
+		for title in "${titles[@]}"; do
+			ktap_test_fail "$label $title"
+		done
+		stop_tool
+		return
+	fi
+	if [ "$mode" = private-shared ] && [ "$action" = reshape ]; then
+		echo "$TARGET" > "$CG/cgroup.procs"
+	fi
+	for stage in 0 1 2; do
+		mask=${COMMON[1]}
+		[ "$stage" = 1 ] || mask+=",$PN"
+		if ! transition_cpuset "$action" "$stage" "$mask"; then
+			ktap_print_msg "cannot change the cpuset"
+			ktap_test_fail "$label ${titles[$stage]}"
+			continue
+		fi
+		report_stage "$stage" "$label ${titles[$stage]}"
+	done
+	wait "$CHILD"
+	CHILD=
+	TARGET=
+}
+
+# Take the private node through stage $1: offline, common, offline, private.
+retype_node()
+{
+	case "$1" in
+	0|2) echo unplugged > "$D/state" ;;
+	1) echo 0 > "$D/private" && echo online_movable > "$D/state" ;;
+	3) echo 1 > "$D/private" && echo online_movable > "$D/state" ;;
+	esac
+}
+
+# A private binding in tool mode $1 while its node is hotplugged and retyped.
+run_private_retype()
+{
+	local mode=$1 label=$2
+	local stage name ready=false
+	local titles=("falls back while the private node is offline"
+		"binds the original node when it returns as common memory"
+		"falls back again after draining the common node"
+		"restores private placement when the node returns as private memory")
+
+	echo "${COMMON[1]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	start_tool "$mode" "$CG" && ready=true
+	for stage in 0 1 2 3; do
+		name="$label ${titles[$stage]}"
+		if [ "$ready" != true ]; then
+			ktap_print_msg "tool is not running"
+			ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		elif ! retype_node "$stage"; then
+			ktap_print_msg "cannot hotplug $(basename "$D")"
+			ktap_test_fail "$name"
+			ready=false
+		elif ! report_stage "$stage" "$name"; then
+			ready=false
+		fi
+	done
+	stop_tool
+	pn_bind_kmem_private "$D"
+}
+
+# A static binding in tool mode $1 of a common node that becomes private.
+run_common_retype()
+{
+	local mode=$1 name=$2 line
+
+	if ! echo unplugged > "$D/state" || ! echo 0 > "$D/private" ||
+	   ! echo online_movable > "$D/state"; then
+		ktap_print_msg "cannot provision common kmem memory"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		return
+	fi
+	echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"
+	if ! start_tool "$mode" "$CG"; then
+		ktap_print_msg "tool setup failed"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		stop_tool
+		return
+	fi
+	if ! echo unplugged > "$D/state" || ! echo 1 > "$D/private" ||
+	   ! echo online_movable > "$D/state" ||
+	   ! echo "${COMMON[1]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems"; then
+		ktap_print_msg "cannot retype kmem memory"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		stop_tool
+		return
+	fi
+	kill -USR1 "$TARGET"
+	if wait "$CHILD"; then
+		line=$(tail -1 "$OUT")
+		ktap_print_msg "$line"
+		if grep -q 'ok=1$' <<<"$line"; then
+			ktap_test_pass "$name"
+		else
+			ktap_test_fail "$name"
+		fi
+	else
+		ktap_print_msg "tool failed or timed out"
+		ktap_test_fail "$name"
+	fi
+	CHILD=
+	TARGET=
+}
+
+pn_setup
+[ -x "$TOOL" ] || pn_skip "kmem_private_rebind_tool not built"
+pn_find_common_nodes 2
+pn_require_mask_nodes "$PN" "${COMMON[@]}"
+pn_cpuset_cgroup "$CG"
+pn_cpuset_cgroup "$CGCOMMON"
+echo "${COMMON[0]},$PN" > "$CG/cpuset.mems" ||
+	ktap_exit_fail_msg "cannot set cpuset.mems of $CG"
+echo "${COMMON[1]}" > "$CGCOMMON/cpuset.mems" ||
+	ktap_exit_fail_msg "cannot set cpuset.mems of $CGCOMMON"
+
+ktap_set_plan 25
+
+run_task_policy interleave
+line=$(tail -1 "$OUT")
+ktap_print_msg "$line"
+name="interleave policy cannot reacquire private memory on rebind"
+if grep -q '^private=0 ' <<<"$line"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+run_task_policy bind
+line=$(tail -1 "$OUT")
+ktap_print_msg "$line"
+name="positional cpuset migration excludes private memory"
+if grep -q '^private=0 ' <<<"$line"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+name="removed common-node pages migrate to common fallback"
+if grep -q ' new_common=64$' <<<"$line"; then
+	ktap_test_pass "$name"
+else
+	ktap_test_fail "$name"
+fi
+
+run_private_transitions private-anon "anonymous binding"
+run_private_transitions private-shared \
+	"shared binding across distinct mapper cpusets"
+run_private_transitions private-anon \
+	"anonymous binding across task attachment" attach
+run_private_transitions private-shared \
+	"shared binding across task attachment" attach
+run_private_retype retype-anon "anonymous private binding"
+run_private_retype retype-shared "shared private binding"
+run_common_retype static \
+	"shared common binding falls back after its node becomes private"
+run_common_retype static-mixed \
+	"shared common binding requires an allowed common target"
+
+ktap_finished

@@ -0,0 +1,495 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+/*
+ * Helper for kmem_private_cpuset.sh and kmem_private_rebind.sh. Most modes
+ * place memory under a policy, print "ready pid=<pid>" and wait for SIGUSR1
+ * while the script changes the cpuset or the node, then report where the
+ * memory went. Modes with several stages wait for one SIGUSR1 per stage and
+ * print one "stage=<n> ... ok=<0|1>" line each.
+ *
+ * Modes that check their own results exit 1 when a check fails. All modes
+ * exit 2 on usage or setup errors.
+ */
+#define _GNU_SOURCE
+#include <linux/mempolicy.h>
+#include <signal.h>
+#include <stdbool.h>
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include <string.h>
+#include <sys/mman.h>
+#include <sys/syscall.h>
+#include <sys/wait.h>
+#include <unistd.h>
+
+#ifndef MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES
+#define MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES (1 << 12)
+#endif
+
+#define NR_PAGES 64
+/* The kernel reads maxnode - 1 bits. */
+#define MAXNODE (8 * sizeof(unsigned long) + 1)
+
+enum mode {
+	ORDINARY,
+	INTERLEAVE,
+	BIND,
+	PRIVATE_ANON,
+	PRIVATE_SHARED,
+	RETYPE_ANON,
+	RETYPE_SHARED,
+	STATIC,
+	STATIC_MIXED,
+	NR_MODES,
+};
+
+static const struct {
+	const char *name;
+	const char *help;
+} modes[NR_MODES] = {
+	[ORDINARY] = { "ordinary", "allocate without a policy" },
+	[INTERLEAVE] = { "interleave",
+			 "task interleave over <private> and <common1>" },
+	[BIND] = { "bind", "task bind to <common1>" },
+	[PRIVATE_ANON] = { "private-anon",
+			   "private binding of anonymous memory" },
+	[PRIVATE_SHARED] = { "private-shared",
+			     "private binding of shared memory, two mappers" },
+	[RETYPE_ANON] = { "retype-anon",
+			  "private-anon across node hotplug" },
+	[RETYPE_SHARED] = { "retype-shared",
+			    "private-shared across node hotplug" },
+	[STATIC] = { "static", "static binding of shared memory to <private>" },
+	[STATIC_MIXED] = { "static-mixed",
+			   "static binding to <private> and <common1>" },
+};
+
+static void print_usage(const char *prog)
+{
+	int i;
+
+	fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s <mode> <private> <common1> <common2>\n",
+		prog);
+	for (i = 0; i < NR_MODES; i++)
+		fprintf(stderr, "  %-15s %s\n", modes[i].name, modes[i].help);
+	exit(2);
+}
+
+/* Node masks are a single unsigned long. */
+static bool node_fits(int nid)
+{
+	return nid >= 0 && nid < (int)(8 * sizeof(unsigned long));
+}
+
+static void *map_anon(long len)
+{
+	return mmap(NULL, len, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
+		    MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
+}
+
+static void *map_shared(int *fd, long len)
+{
+	*fd = memfd_create("private-rebind", 0);
+	if (*fd < 0 || ftruncate(*fd, len))
+		return MAP_FAILED;
+	return mmap(NULL, len, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, *fd, 0);
+}
+
+static void announce_ready(void)
+{
+	printf("ready pid=%d\n", getpid());
+	fflush(stdout);
+}
+
+static long count_node(void *addr, long page_size, int nid)
+{
+	void *pages[NR_PAGES];
+	int status[NR_PAGES];
+	long i, count = 0;
+
+	for (i = 0; i < NR_PAGES; i++)
+		pages[i] = addr + i * page_size;
+	if (syscall(SYS_move_pages, 0, NR_PAGES, pages, NULL, status, 0UL))
+		return -1;
+	for (i = 0; i < NR_PAGES; i++)
+		count += status[i] == nid;
+	return count;
+}
+
+static bool range_matches(void *ptr, long page_size, unsigned char value)
+{
+	long i;
+
+	for (i = 0; i < NR_PAGES; i++)
+		if (*(unsigned char *)(ptr + i * page_size) != value)
+			return false;
+	return true;
+}
+
+static int bind_mapping(void *ptr, long len, unsigned long mask, int flags)
+{
+	return syscall(SYS_mbind, ptr, len, MPOL_BIND | flags,
+		       &mask, MAXNODE, 0UL);
+}
+
+static bool policy_matches(void *ptr, unsigned long mask, int flags)
+{
+	unsigned long actual = 0;
+	int mode;
+
+	return !syscall(SYS_get_mempolicy, &mode, &actual, MAXNODE,
+			ptr, MPOL_F_ADDR) &&
+		mode == (MPOL_BIND | flags) && actual == mask;
+}
+
+/* Report how many pages are on the private node. */
+static int ordinary(long page_size, int priv)
+{
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	void *ptr = map_anon(len);
+
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED)
+		return 2;
+	memset(ptr, 0xab, len);
+	printf("private=%ld\n", count_node(ptr, page_size, priv));
+	return 0;
+}
+
+static void report_placement(void *ptr, long page_size, int priv,
+			     int common1, int common2)
+{
+	printf("private=%ld old_common=%ld new_common=%ld\n",
+	       count_node(ptr, page_size, priv),
+	       count_node(ptr, page_size, common1),
+	       count_node(ptr, page_size, common2));
+}
+
+/* Interleave over the private node and allocate after the cpuset change. */
+static int task_interleave(long page_size, int priv, int common1,
+			   int common2, const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = (1UL << common1) | (1UL << priv);
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	void *ptr;
+	int sig;
+
+	if (syscall(SYS_set_mempolicy, MPOL_INTERLEAVE, &mask, MAXNODE))
+		return 2;
+	announce_ready();
+	sigwait(waitset, &sig);
+	ptr = map_anon(len);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED)
+		return 2;
+	memset(ptr, 0xcd, len);
+	report_placement(ptr, page_size, priv, common1, common2);
+	munmap(ptr, len);
+	return 0;
+}
+
+/* Bind to the first common node and allocate before the cpuset change. */
+static int task_bind(long page_size, int priv, int common1, int common2,
+		     const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = 1UL << common1;
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	void *ptr;
+	int sig;
+
+	if (syscall(SYS_set_mempolicy, MPOL_BIND, &mask, MAXNODE))
+		return 2;
+	ptr = map_anon(len);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED)
+		return 2;
+	memset(ptr, 0xab, len);
+	announce_ready();
+	sigwait(waitset, &sig);
+	report_placement(ptr, page_size, priv, common1, common2);
+	munmap(ptr, len);
+	return 0;
+}
+
+struct shared_result {
+	long private_pages;
+	long shared_pages;
+};
+
+/* Keep one mapper outside the cpuset that is being changed. */
+static int shared_mapper(void *ptr, long len, long page_size, int priv,
+			 int common, int requests, int replies, pid_t child)
+{
+	struct shared_result result;
+	int stage, status;
+	bool contents;
+	void *range;
+
+	while (read(requests, &stage, sizeof(stage)) == sizeof(stage)) {
+		range = ptr + (stage + 4) * len;
+		memset(range, 0xef, len);
+		result.private_pages = count_node(range, page_size, priv);
+
+		/* Existing shared pages are not reallocated for another mapper. */
+		range = ptr + (stage + 1) * len;
+		contents = range_matches(range, page_size, 0xcd);
+		result.shared_pages = count_node(range, page_size,
+						 stage == 1 ? common : priv);
+		if (!contents)
+			result.shared_pages = -1;
+		if (write(replies, &result, sizeof(result)) != sizeof(result))
+			break;
+	}
+	close(requests);
+	close(replies);
+	if (waitpid(child, &status, 0) != child || !WIFEXITED(status))
+		return 1;
+	return WEXITSTATUS(status);
+}
+
+/*
+ * A private binding across three cpuset changes that allow, revoke and allow
+ * the node again. Range 0 of the mapping is populated up front and range
+ * 1 + stage at each stage. For shared memory the parent stays outside the
+ * cpuset as a second mapper and populates range 4 + stage.
+ */
+static int private_rebind(bool shared, long page_size, int priv, int common,
+			  const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = 1UL << priv;
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	long total = (shared ? 7 : 4) * len;
+	int fd = -1, requests[2], replies[2];
+	int stage, sig, failed = 0;
+	struct shared_result other;
+	long private_pages, common_pages, existing, existing_common;
+	bool policy, contents, ok;
+	pid_t child;
+	void *ptr, *range;
+
+	if (shared)
+		ptr = map_shared(&fd, total);
+	else
+		ptr = map_anon(total);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED ||
+	    bind_mapping(ptr, total, mask, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES))
+		return 2;
+	/* Keep later ranges absent until their respective cpuset transition. */
+	if (madvise(ptr, total, MADV_NOHUGEPAGE))
+		return 2;
+	memset(ptr, 0xab, len);
+	if (count_node(ptr, page_size, priv) != NR_PAGES)
+		return 1;
+
+	if (shared) {
+		if (pipe(requests) || pipe(replies))
+			return 2;
+		child = fork();
+		if (child < 0)
+			return 2;
+		if (child) {
+			close(requests[1]);
+			close(replies[0]);
+			failed = shared_mapper(ptr, len, page_size, priv, common,
+					       requests[0], replies[1], child);
+			goto out;
+		}
+		close(requests[0]);
+		close(replies[1]);
+		/* Populate the child's PTEs before cpuset-requested migration. */
+		if (!range_matches(ptr, page_size, 0xab))
+			return 2;
+	}
+
+	announce_ready();
+	for (stage = 0; stage < 3; stage++) {
+		if (sigwait(waitset, &sig))
+			return 2;
+		range = ptr + (stage + 1) * len;
+		memset(range, 0xcd, len);
+		private_pages = count_node(range, page_size, priv);
+		common_pages = count_node(range, page_size, common);
+		/* File-backed PTEs can be populated lazily after fork. */
+		contents = range_matches(ptr, page_size, 0xab);
+		existing = count_node(ptr, page_size, priv);
+		existing_common = count_node(ptr, page_size, common);
+		policy = policy_matches(ptr, mask, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES);
+		ok = policy && contents;
+		/* Old pages leave the private node only once it is revoked. */
+		if (stage == 0)
+			ok &= existing == NR_PAGES && existing_common == 0;
+		else
+			ok &= existing == 0 && existing_common == NR_PAGES;
+		if (stage == 1)
+			ok &= common_pages == NR_PAGES && private_pages == 0;
+		else
+			ok &= private_pages == NR_PAGES && common_pages == 0;
+		other.private_pages = -1;
+		other.shared_pages = -1;
+		if (shared) {
+			if (write(requests[1], &stage, sizeof(stage)) != sizeof(stage) ||
+			    read(replies[0], &other, sizeof(other)) != sizeof(other))
+				return 2;
+			ok &= other.private_pages == NR_PAGES &&
+				other.shared_pages == NR_PAGES;
+		}
+		printf("stage=%d private=%ld common=%ld existing_private=%ld ",
+		       stage, private_pages, common_pages, existing);
+		printf("existing_common=%ld ", existing_common);
+		printf("policy=%d other_private=%ld shared_pages=%ld ok=%d\n",
+		       policy, other.private_pages, other.shared_pages, ok);
+		fflush(stdout);
+		failed |= !ok;
+	}
+	if (shared) {
+		close(requests[1]);
+		close(replies[0]);
+	}
+out:
+	munmap(ptr, total);
+	if (fd >= 0)
+		close(fd);
+	return failed;
+}
+
+/*
+ * A private binding while the node goes offline, returns as common memory,
+ * goes offline again and returns as private memory. Range @stage of the
+ * mapping is populated at each stage.
+ */
+static int private_retype(bool shared, long page_size, int target, int common,
+			  const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = 1UL << target;
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	long private_pages, common_pages;
+	int fd = -1, stage, sig, i, failed = 0;
+	bool policy, contents, ok;
+	void *ptr, *range;
+
+	if (shared)
+		ptr = map_shared(&fd, 4 * len);
+	else
+		ptr = map_anon(4 * len);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED ||
+	    bind_mapping(ptr, 4 * len, mask, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES) ||
+	    madvise(ptr, 4 * len, MADV_NOHUGEPAGE))
+		return 2;
+
+	/* Keep the policy alive without preventing the initial hot-unplug. */
+	announce_ready();
+	for (stage = 0; stage < 4; stage++) {
+		if (sigwait(waitset, &sig))
+			return 2;
+		range = ptr + stage * len;
+		memset(range, 0xa0 + stage, len);
+		private_pages = count_node(range, page_size, target);
+		common_pages = count_node(range, page_size, common);
+		policy = policy_matches(ptr, mask, MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES);
+		contents = true;
+		for (i = 0; i <= stage; i++)
+			contents &= range_matches(ptr + i * len, page_size,
+						  0xa0 + i);
+		ok = policy && contents;
+		if (stage & 1)
+			ok &= private_pages == NR_PAGES && common_pages == 0;
+		else
+			ok &= private_pages == 0 && common_pages == NR_PAGES;
+		printf("stage=%d target=%ld common=%ld policy=%d contents=%d ok=%d\n",
+		       stage, private_pages, common_pages, policy, contents, ok);
+		fflush(stdout);
+		failed |= !ok;
+	}
+	munmap(ptr, 4 * len);
+	if (fd >= 0)
+		close(fd);
+	return failed;
+}
+
+/*
+ * A static binding of shared memory to a common node, optionally with a
+ * second common node, that the script turns private before a second mapper
+ * faults the pages in.
+ */
+static int common_retype(bool mixed, long page_size, int target,
+			 int old_common, int new_common,
+			 const sigset_t *waitset)
+{
+	unsigned long mask = 1UL << target;
+	long len = NR_PAGES * page_size;
+	long private_pages, common_pages;
+	int fd, sig;
+	bool policy, ok;
+	void *ptr, *other;
+
+	if (mixed)
+		mask |= 1UL << old_common;
+	ptr = map_shared(&fd, len);
+	if (ptr == MAP_FAILED ||
+	    bind_mapping(ptr, len, mask, MPOL_F_STATIC_NODES))
+		return 2;
+	other = mmap(NULL, len, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
+	if (other == MAP_FAILED)
+		return 2;
+	/* No resident pages: the target can be removed and retyped. */
+	announce_ready();
+	if (sigwait(waitset, &sig))
+		return 2;
+	memset(other, 0xcd, len);
+	private_pages = count_node(other, page_size, target);
+	common_pages = count_node(other, page_size, new_common);
+	policy = policy_matches(other, mask, MPOL_F_STATIC_NODES);
+	ok = private_pages == 0 && common_pages == NR_PAGES && policy;
+	printf("private=%ld common=%ld policy=%d ok=%d\n",
+	       private_pages, common_pages, policy, ok);
+	munmap(other, len);
+	munmap(ptr, len);
+	close(fd);
+	return !ok;
+}
+
+int main(int argc, char **argv)
+{
+	long page_size = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
+	int priv, common1, common2, mode;
+	sigset_t waitset;
+
+	if (argc != 5)
+		print_usage(argv[0]);
+	for (mode = 0; mode < NR_MODES; mode++)
+		if (!strcmp(argv[1], modes[mode].name))
+			break;
+	if (mode == NR_MODES)
+		print_usage(argv[0]);
+	priv = atoi(argv[2]);
+	common1 = atoi(argv[3]);
+	common2 = atoi(argv[4]);
+	if (!node_fits(priv) || !node_fits(common1) || !node_fits(common2)) {
+		fprintf(stderr, "node ids must be 0 to %zu\n",
+			8 * sizeof(unsigned long) - 1);
+		return 2;
+	}
+
+	sigemptyset(&waitset);
+	sigaddset(&waitset, SIGUSR1);
+	sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, &waitset, NULL);
+
+	switch (mode) {
+	case ORDINARY:
+		return ordinary(page_size, priv);
+	case INTERLEAVE:
+		return task_interleave(page_size, priv, common1, common2,
+				       &waitset);
+	case BIND:
+		return task_bind(page_size, priv, common1, common2, &waitset);
+	case PRIVATE_ANON:
+	case PRIVATE_SHARED:
+		return private_rebind(mode == PRIVATE_SHARED, page_size, priv,
+				      common2, &waitset);
+	case RETYPE_ANON:
+	case RETYPE_SHARED:
+		return private_retype(mode == RETYPE_SHARED, page_size, priv,
+				      common2, &waitset);
+	case STATIC:
+	case STATIC_MIXED:
+		return common_retype(mode == STATIC_MIXED, page_size, priv,
+				     common1, common2, &waitset);
+	}
+	return 2;
+}

series_items.subject: [PATCH 60/60] Documentation/mm: describe private memory nodes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds documentation to describe private memory nodes, including how to create and manage them using DAX kmem private mode, binding memory to them, controlling access with cpusets, handling node unavailability or fullness, shared memory placement, and memory management services. It also updates the cgroup guides to reflect that cpuset memory migration never targets a private node and only moves pages off when the cpuset no longer allows it.

review_comments.author: Gregory Relay

From: "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net>

Add Documentation/mm/numa_private_nodes.rst for administrators,
covering:
  - creating a private node with dax kmem private mode.
  - binding memory to it with MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES, and explicit
    migration.
  - controlling access with cpusets.
  - what happens when the node becomes unavailable or full.
  - shared memory placement.
  - which memory management services apply, and how memory counters
    account private memory.

In both cgroup guides, document that cpuset memory migration never
targets a private node and moves pages off one only when the cpuset no
longer allows it. Document how a private-only cpuset.mems gains the
parent's common memory nodes in v2, and is rejected in v1.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

index 000000000000..2fedf7534446
--- /dev/null
+++ b/Documentation/mm/numa_private_nodes.rst
@@ -0,0 +1,223 @@
+.. SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+
+====================
+Private memory nodes
+====================
+
+A private memory node is a NUMA node whose memory the kernel does not use for
+ordinary allocations. Applications place memory there only by asking for that
+node explicitly. This keeps specialized memory, such as HBM or coherent device
+memory, visible as a NUMA node without making it a general fallback for every
+allocation. Memory that is not private is called common memory.
+
+The kernel manages a private node's memory with the usual page allocator. The
+driver that provides the memory decides which memory management services the
+node also gets. The dax kmem private mode described below enables reclaim,
+compaction and explicit placement by applications.
+
+``/sys/devices/system/node/has_private_memory`` lists the private nodes, and
+``has_common_memory`` lists the others. Together they make up ``has_memory``.
+
+Creating a private node
+=======================
+
+Private memory is added through memory hotplug and requires ``CONFIG_NUMA``.
+With ``CONFIG_DEV_DAX_KMEM`` and ``CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE``, a device-dax
+instance bound to ``kmem`` can be onlined as private memory. Select private mode
+while the device's memory is unplugged::
+
+    echo unplugged > /sys/bus/dax/devices/daxX.Y/state
+    echo 1 > /sys/bus/dax/devices/daxX.Y/private
+    echo online_movable > /sys/bus/dax/devices/daxX.Y/state
+
+The ``private`` attribute defaults to 0, which keeps ordinary kmem behavior.
+Its value can change only while the device is unplugged. Unbinding kmem
+discards the setting. Bind the device with memory auto-onlining disabled, so
+that its memory is not onlined as common memory first.
+
+All System RAM on a node shares one configuration. Adding memory with a
+different configuration to a node that already has System RAM fails with
+``-EBUSY``. To change the configuration, remove every System RAM block on the
+node first. Offlining the blocks is not enough, since offline blocks keep their
+configuration so they can be onlined again.
+
+A private node may have CPUs. Like the CPUs of a memoryless node, they get
+ordinary memory from the nearest common nodes.
+
+Using private memory
+====================
+
+An application binds an anonymous or shmem-backed mapping to one private node
+with ``mbind(2)``, passing ``MPOL_BIND | MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES``, before it
+faults the pages in::
+
+    buf = mmap(NULL, length, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
+               MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
+    /* mask contains exactly the chosen private node */
+    mbind(buf, length, MPOL_BIND | MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES, mask, maxnode, 0);
+    memset(buf, 0, length);
+
+``mbind(2)`` rejects a private binding with ``-EINVAL`` if:
+
+- the mask names more than one node, or a node that is not private memory
+  with userspace placement enabled.
+- the mode is not ``MPOL_BIND``, or the flag is combined with
+  ``MPOL_F_STATIC_NODES``, ``MPOL_F_RELATIVE_NODES`` or
+  ``MPOL_F_NUMA_BALANCING``.
+- the mapping is a HugeTLB mapping. Private nodes hold no HugeTLB pages.
+- the node is not in the caller's cpuset.
+
+Kernels without private node support reject the flag with ``-EINVAL``, so
+applications can probe for it. ``get_mempolicy(2)`` reports the flag.
+
+Without ``MPOL_F_PRIVATE_NODES``, private nodes in a ``set_mempolicy(2)`` or
+``mbind(2)`` mask are ignored, as nodes outside the cpuset are. A mask that
+names only private nodes is therefore rejected with ``-EINVAL``.
+``set_mempolicy(2)`` does not accept the flag, because a task policy also
+applies to the kernel's allocations on behalf of the task. Preferred,
+interleave and preferred-many policies, tmpfs ``mpol=`` mount options, HugeTLB
+pools and automatic NUMA balancing use only common memory.
+
+``move_pages(2)`` and ``migrate_pages(2)`` can move pages to a private node
+with userspace placement enabled, subject to their usual permission checks.
+They take no flag. ``move_pages(2)`` rejects other private nodes with
+``-ENODEV``, and ``migrate_pages(2)`` ignores them, as it ignores nodes outside
+the caller's cpuset.
+
+Page cache for regular files is never allocated from private memory.
+Copy-on-write pages of a private file mapping follow a binding like anonymous
+memory, and explicit migration can move existing file pages to a private node.
+A private binding on a shmem-backed mapping allocates its pages from the
+private node, and reclaim swaps them out like other shmem pages.
+
+guest_memfd memory cannot be moved, so a binding places it on a private node
+only if the node has memory onlined as ``online`` or ``online_kernel``.
+
+Controlling access
+==================
+
+``cpuset.mems`` includes private nodes by default, so any task can bind to a
+private node and use up its capacity. Use ``cpuset.mems`` to limit which tasks
+may use a private node. Listing a private node in ``cpuset.mems`` permits
+private bindings to it. Tasks do not otherwise allocate from it.
+
+In cgroup v2, a ``cpuset.mems`` that names only private nodes is accepted, and
+the parent's common nodes are added to ``cpuset.mems.effective`` so that tasks
+always have memory for ordinary allocations. The parent's other private nodes
+are not added. An empty ``cpuset.mems`` inherits the parent's effective nodes,
+private nodes included.
+
+In cgroup v1, writing a ``cpuset.mems`` that names only private nodes, or
+attaching a task to such a cpuset, fails with ``-ENOSPC``. When memory hotplug
+leaves a v1 cpuset with only private memory, its tasks move to an ancestor.
+
+Cpuset memory migration never moves pages to a private node. It moves pages
+off a private node only when the cpuset no longer allows that node.
+
+When a node becomes unavailable
+===============================
+
+A private binding applies while its node is online private memory with
+userspace placement enabled and the task's cpuset allows it. While it applies,
+allocations use only that node and never fall back to common memory.
+
+Otherwise the binding is suspended and allocations use the task's common
+memory. The binding is never rebound to another node. It applies again when
+its node becomes available again. If the node comes back as common memory, the
+binding acts like an ordinary binding to that node. ``get_mempolicy(2)`` keeps
+reporting the original binding throughout.
+
+==============================  ==================  =========================
+Event                           New allocations     Existing private pages
+==============================  ==================  =========================
+cpuset removes the node         common memory       migrated to common memory
+cpuset allows the node again    the private node    not migrated back
+node is being hot-removed       the private node    migrated to common memory
+node is removed                 common memory       none remain
+node returns as private memory  the private node
+node returns as common memory   that common node
+==============================  ==================  =========================
+
+While a node is being hot-removed, its free memory is no longer available, so
+faults on mappings bound to it can fail with ``SIGBUS`` until removal finishes.
+
+Allocations that cannot use ``ZONE_MOVABLE``, such as guest_memfd memory, ignore
+a binding to a private node whose memory is all movable and use common memory.
+Long-term pins migrate pages out of ``ZONE_MOVABLE`` as usual.
+
+An ordinary policy that is not rebound, such as a static binding or a shared
+memory policy, can name a node that later comes back as private memory. If the
+task may use no common node in such a policy, the policy is ignored and the
+allocation uses common memory.
+
+Exhaustion and OOM
+==================
+
+A private node is a fixed pool, like a HugeTLB pool. When the node is full and
+reclaim cannot free enough memory on it, an allocation for a private binding
+fails without invoking the OOM killer and without falling back to common
+memory. A page fault then gets ``SIGBUS``, as with an exhausted HugeTLB pool.
+Other callers see an error, such as ``-ENOMEM`` from ``write(2)`` to a shmem
+file or ``-EFAULT`` from a write through ``/proc/pid/mem`` or
+``process_vm_writev(2)``. Allocations succeed again once memory on the node is
+freed.
+
+Private pages are charged to memory cgroups like other memory. Reaching a
+memory cgroup limit causes reclaim and OOM handling as usual, and memcg reclaim
+also reclaims private nodes that permit reclaim.
+
+Tasks whose cpusets overlap only on private nodes are not chosen as OOM victims
+for each other.
+
+Shared memory
+=============
+
+A private binding on a shmem-backed mapping, such as memfd, tmpfs or shared
+anonymous memory, applies to the file's offset range, not to each task that
+maps it. Whether a new page is allocated on the private node depends on the
+cpuset of the task that faults it in. A task whose cpuset excludes the node
+allocates the page on common memory, and every task that maps the file then
+uses that page. A file can therefore hold both private and common pages.
+
+Shared pages keep using private memory until they are freed. Unmapping the
+file does not free them while the file still exists or another task keeps it
+open. Truncate the file or punch holes in it to return the memory.
+
+Memory management services
+==========================
+
+kswapd and kcompactd run on a private node only if its driver enables reclaim
+and compaction, as the dax kmem private mode does. Writing to ``nodeN/reclaim``
+or ``nodeN/compact`` fails with ``-EOPNOTSUPP`` for a private node without the
+service. ``MADV_COLD``, ``MADV_PAGEOUT`` and ``MADV_FREE`` act only on pages on
+nodes that permit reclaim.
+
+Private nodes are excluded from KSM merging, THP collapse, automatic NUMA
+balancing, DAMON actions, demotion between memory tiers and HugeTLB pool
+growth. A KSM page that is explicitly migrated to a private node remains
+shareable while it is mapped.
+
+Memory hot-remove and soft offline migrate pages on a private node to common
+memory. Pinned or otherwise unmovable pages can still prevent removal.
+
+Accounting
+==========
+
+``MemTotal`` and ``MemFree`` in ``/proc/meminfo`` include private memory with
+userspace placement enabled, such as dax kmem private memory, since it holds
+ordinary application data. They leave out other private memory. The overcommit
+limit (``CommitLimit``) and other limits sized from total memory follow
+``MemTotal``.
+
+``MemAvailable`` and the dirty page limits count free memory on common nodes
+only, since free private memory serves only private bindings. ``MemTotal``
+minus ``MemAvailable`` therefore includes free private memory.
+
+Per-node statistics, including ``nodeN/meminfo``, ``/proc/vmstat`` and
+``memory.numa_stat``, count all memory, private memory included.
+
+Limitations
+===========
+
